name: Anushirvan Sharaf al-Ma'ali
summary:
Anushirvan Sharaf al-Ma'ali was the ruler of the Ziyarids from 1035 to 1040. He ascended to the throne after the death of his father, Manuchihr.

Born into a prominent noble family in ancient Iran, Anushirvan's reign saw significant military campaigns against neighboring tribes and empires. The core events of his rule included the establishment of trade relations with Byzantium and the expansion of Ziyarid influence into Eastern Anatolia.

Anushirvan's legacy can be seen in the continued regional dominance of the Ziyarids for generations to come, as well as the lasting impact on the cultural landscape of the Caucasus region. The historian Tabari described Anushirvan as a 'great king' who brought peace and prosperity to his people.

The historical importance of Anushirvan Sharaf al-Ma'ali lies in his significant regional influence during a time of great upheaval, where the Ziyarid kingdom played a crucial role in shaping the destiny of the region. His reign saw the establishment of trade relations with Byzantium and the expansion of Ziyarid influence into Eastern Anatolia.
